item.title: SEC questions REX-Osprey’s launch of Ethereum and Solana collateralized ETFs
item.description: Mars Finance News: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) warned REX Shares and Osprey Funds on Friday night that their proposed staking Ethereum and Solana ETF products may not meet the definition of an "investment company" under the Investment Company Act and fail to satisfy the legal compliance requirements for ETFs. The two companies previously submitted registration statements, intending to create funds through a C-corporation structure with at least 50% of assets used for staking to obtain additional returns. Bloomberg analyst James Seyffart said the proposal employed "multiple clever legal and regulatory evasion strategies". The SEC noted in its letter that the registration statement would take effect before some "unresolved issues" are resolved, violating procedures, and has requested issuers to postpone its effectiveness. SEC Assistant Director Brent J. Fields stated that if issues remain unresolved, the SEC will consider enforcement or mandatory resubmission. Greg Collett, REX Financial General Counsel, told Bloomberg that the company will not launch the product before meeting SEC requirements. Notably, spot Ethereum ETFs have been trading since last July, but spot Solana ETFs have not yet been approved, thus facing double regulatory obstacles. (The Block)

item.title: BlackRock's IBIT Bitcoin Spot ETF's 34-day streak of net inflows ended with a single-day outflow of $430 million
item.description: Mars Finance News: BlackRock's IBIT, the world's largest Bitcoin spot ETF, experienced a $430 million outflow on Friday, ending its previous 34-day consecutive net inflow record (including 3 days of zero inflow). During the same period, the total net outflow of all Bitcoin spot ETFs in the US stock market reached $616 million, the largest single-day outflow since February 26, against the backdrop of BTC price dropping about 4% in five days. Despite the capital outflow, IBIT's market dominance remains solid, with assets under management reaching $69.2 billion, approximately 3.3 times that of Fidelity's FBTC (at $20.8 billion). Currently, IBIT accounts for 3.33% of the total Bitcoin circulation, far exceeding FBTC's 1%. Data shows that IBIT maintains around 80% of the trading volume among all Bitcoin ETFs. Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas noted that IBIT recently occupied "over 100%" of all fund inflows, indicating that the recent market is more driven by institutions rather than retail investor enthusiasm. ETF Store President Nate Geraci commented: "In less than 17 months, IBIT's assets are approaching $70 billion, which is simply incredible." (The Block)

item.title: Bitcoin advocates question the ability of new BTC finance companies to withstand pressure, saying they have not experienced the test of a bear market
item.description:
<odaily> Planet Daily News: Bitcoin advocate Max Keiser criticized Bitcoin treasury companies that recently imitated MicroStrategy's model on May 30th, questioning their ability to maintain financial discipline during a prolonged bear market. He stated that while Michael Saylor continued to accumulate and never sold during past bear markets, many "strategy clone companies" have not experienced similar market conditions and may not demonstrate the same steadfast holding attitude if faced with a pullback.
Keiser wrote: "Saylor never sold even when at a loss and continued buying. It would be foolish to think the new generation of BTC treasury companies would have the same discipline. 'Strategy is the Bitcoin itself in Bitcoin financial operations', act accordingly."
After MicroStrategy's stock price surged significantly and reached a high of $543, dozens of strategy imitators emerged. For example, asset management company Strive (founded by Vivek Ramaswamy) announced a BTC reserve strategy on May 7th, and Trump's media technology company TMTG announced raising $2.5 billion for Bitcoin purchases on May 27th.
Additional analysis pointed out that Metaplanet currently has a premium of $600,000, with investors paying nearly six times the cost of directly purchasing BTC to gain BTC exposure, a premium risk worth noting.</odaily>

item.description: <odaily> Planet News: Loud! (LOUD) has completed two stages of token sale. item.title: James Wynn: It's all or nothing, he has no intention of cashing in on $100 million in profits
item.description:
On June 1st, whale James Wynn again posted that he will make a comeback, "I don't want to delve deep into this topic, but let me briefly mention it.

For those who say I made $100 million and then lost it all, such statements are too common in the crypto circle. I leveraged my trades from $3-4 million to nearly $100 million in profit, and then ultimately lost $13 million. Some of you act like gods, thinking you would cash out at $100 million. Have you ever considered that I never intended to cash out at $100 million? Why would I cash out?"

"Here's some perspective: Sometimes $10,000 can change a person's life, sometimes $100,000, sometimes $1 million, sometimes $10 million, sometimes $100 million, and sometimes even $1 billion or $10 billion. Everyone has their own track, everyone has their own goals. For me, it's either win everything or lose everything. But my 'nothing' is still a happy state. So I don't encourage anyone to follow my high-risk approach. But no matter what, I will make a comeback and reclaim everything. James Wynn will return, but I'll wait until no one is prepared, including those corrupt market makers who have directly attacked me multiple times. My timing was wrong, and their selling power was too strong at that time. That's all, have a great weekend!"

Earlier today, James Wynn closed his BTC 40x leverage and PEPE 10x leverage long positions, losing $2.81 million. Currently, James Wynn holds no positions, with total losses reaching $17.72 million. He transferred approximately 464,000 USDC from HyperLiquid, leaving his account empty of stablecoins.

item.title: 1confirmation founder: There is a huge difference between trusted neutral value storage and corporate currency, but most people are keen to speculate ...
item.description: Mars Finance News: Nick Tomaino, founder of 1confirmation, posted on X platform that there is a huge difference between credibly neutral value storage and "company coins", and understanding this is key to getting rich or going broke in cryptocurrency. 1. Company coins have high internal shareholding ratios, highly coordinated marketing narratives, and jurisdictional constraints. Early purchases can make you a fortune, but you must time it right and sell before the market ultimately ends. Value depends on revenue (like a company), with limited upside potential. Hype is always intense, but there are always new shiny targets worth chasing. 2. Credibly neutral value storage methods have lower internal shareholding ratios, effective global early ownership distribution mechanisms, decentralized marketing, and are not constrained by jurisdictions. Value is based on belief, requiring steadfast believers willing to hold the asset over any other asset in the world. Credibly neutral value storage is the most globally promising investment opportunity, with potential market value exceeding $100 trillion. However, most people tend to dive in headfirst, over-investing in company coins while paying insufficient attention to credibly neutral value storage tools.

item.title: Analysis: ETH/BTC is forming multiple bullish technical patterns, which may trigger a new round of altcoin season
item.description: <odaily> Planet Daily News: ETH/BTC is forming multiple bullish technical patterns, with analysts believing this could trigger a new "Altcoin season" in 2025. Technically, the ETH/BTC ratio is showing both a cup and handle formation and a bullish flag pattern. The cup and handle formation suggests a potential breakthrough of the 0.02596 BTC neckline, with a technical target near 0.03814 BTC, implying a possible 55% increase by July. The bullish flag pattern indicates a potential breakthrough to 0.03235 BTC, approximately 30% higher than the current level. Analyst Trader Tardigrade suggests that an ETH/BTC breakthrough could spark the 2025 Altcoin season. Data shown by analyst Sensei indicates that the market cap of Altcoins relative to Bitcoin is retesting a long-term ascending support trend line. Historically, each rebound from this level has signaled massive Altcoin rallies, with one leading to a 9,000% surge and another triggering a 180,000% market cap explosion. Analyst Moustache also points out that Altcoins are breaking through a seven-year descending wedge, a pattern that appeared before significant rallies in 2017 and 2020, suggesting a new Altcoin season may be imminent. (Cointelegraph)</odaily>

item.title: Several insurance companies plan to launch crypto asset kidnapping insurance to cover violent threats against crypto tycoons
item.description: Mars Finance News, on May 31, according to Cointelegraph, at least three professional insurance institutions are developing customized kidnapping and ransom (K&R) insurance for crypto asset investors, with the first batch of products expected to be launched this fall. Recently, violent threat cases against crypto-rich individuals have been frequent, with the Noizat family, co-founder of French trading platform Paymium, experiencing a kidnapping attempt, and a robbery involving $730,000 occurring in Seoul, South Korea, under the guise of a crypto transaction. According to a report by private security company Infinite Risks International, bodyguard demand for crypto-rich individuals has surged 300% year-on-year since May. Rebecca Rubenfeld, COO of AnchorWatch Insurance, stated at the Bitcoin 2025 conference that they will launch a crypto-specific customized kidnapping and ransom insurance product in the fall. Andrew Kurt, Vice President of Hylant Capital, commented, "This is not a high-frequency risk, but an extremely severe event, similar to corporate executive kidnapping insurance, where one case in ten years might occur, but that single case could result in a loss of millions of dollars."
